title: Background task notifications trigger autonomous API calls — model responds as if it were the user
body:
## Bug: Background task notifications trigger autonomous API calls with `bypassPermissions` — model responds as if it were the user ### Summary When a background task (launched via `run_in_background`) completes while the REPL is idle, Claude Code materializes the task-notification as a synthetic `type: "user"` message with `permissionMode: "bypassPermissions"` and sends the full conversation history to the Claude API. The model then generates a response to this synthetic turn — with no user interaction, no permission prompts, and full tool access. If there is a **pending question** in the conversation when the notification arrives, the model may answer its own question on the user's behalf, impersonating the user's intent. ### Severity **High.** The autonomous response runs with `bypassPermissions`, meaning the model can execute arbitrary tool calls (Bash, Write, Edit, etc.) without any user confirmation. The model has no system-level instruction distinguishing task-notification turns from real human input. ### Reproduction
Steps to reproduce 1. Start a Claude Code session 2. Run a command with `run_in_background: true` (e.g., `inotifywait`, `sleep 10 && echo done`, any background task) 3. While the task is running, ask Claude a yes/no question or present it with a decision 4. Wait for the background task to complete before responding yourself 5. Observe: Claude generates an autonomous response, potentially "answering" its own question
### What happens
Full end-to-end trace from session transcript **Step 1** — Assistant asks a question (UUID `ca9ef575`): > Want me to go ahead and remove it from `~/.claude/settings.json`? **Step 2** — Background task completes 5 seconds later. Claude Code enqueues and dequeues the notification: ```json {"type":"queue-operation","operation":"enqueue","timestamp":"2026-03-25T22:31:01.660Z", "content":"\nbj2fzmtsf..."} {"type":"queue-operation","operation":"dequeue","timestamp":"2026-03-25T22:31:01.669Z"} ``` **Step 3** — Claude Code materializes the notification as a **synthetic user message**: ```json { "type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "..."}, "permissionMode": "bypassPermissions", "origin": {"kind": "task-notification"}, "uuid": "22acb7c4-..." } ``` **Step 4** — A **new API call** is made (different `requestId`). Claude sees the conversation ending with its own pending question followed by this synthetic user turn, and generates: ```json { "type": "assistant", "message": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Yeah remove it, I don't need the frame timing data."}]}, "requestId": "req_011CZQbDZGeS2aasvGUKZfdk", "uuid": "5e1246cb-..." } ``` The model **impersonated the user**, answering its own question with a first-person instruction. The task-notification content (inotifywait output about a file being modified) contained no such instruction — the model hallucinated it from the conversational context.
### Scope of impact This is **not version-specific**. Searching across 419 session transcripts: | Version | Sessions affected | Autonomous text responses | Notes | |---------|:-:|:-:|-------| | 2.1.50 | 1 | 8 | Network capture session — 8 autonomous responses in one session | | 2.1.70 | 1 | 1 | “Prompt is too long” | | 2.1.72 | 1 | 2 | “Looks good to file?” — asked a follow-up question autonomously | | 2.1.76 | 3 | 4 | Status acknowledgments | | 2.1.80 | 1 | 1 | Status acknowledgment | | 2.1.81 | 3 | 3 | Includes “Go ahead” — autonomous green-light | | 2.1.83 | 3 | 3 | Includes the impersonation case | | **Total** | **13** | **22** | Across 8 versions, going back to at least 2.1.50 | The notification **inherits the session’s active permission mode** — it does not force any specific mode.
